body:
MEASURED 2026-08-18, and already half-known: tests.yml:45-49 says "Twice observed
stalling in the apt step" and caps the job at timeout-minutes: 25 so a stall cannot run
to GitHub's 6-hour default. The cap works. What it does not do is stop the stall from
costing a full 25 minutes and then presenting as something it is not.

Observed today on run 32169649515 (PR #1743, head 9f9b8ee59), per-step timings:
  step  7  Install system dependencies   18:12:32 .. 18:36:52  CANCELLED  (24m20s)
  step 10  Run smoke and unit tests      18:36:52 .. 18:36:52  SKIPPED
The tests never executed. Independently on #1745 the same step was still in apt after
~40 minutes. So four-plus occurrences now, not two.

Why it costs more than the wasted minutes — the reporting chain launders it into a code
failure:
  apt stalls -> job hits timeout-minutes -> GitHub reports the job CANCELLED (a job killed
  by its own timeout is never reported as `failure`; tests.yml:1016 documents this) ->
  Test Suite Summary correctly refuses to pass a non-success result (#1727) -> `gh pr
  checks` renders the cancelled run as `fail`.
The PR therefore shows "Fast Tests = fail" for a run in which NO TEST RAN. I read that
today and began investigating whether the PR's own change had broken the suite. It had
not, and nothing in the surfaced signal said so.

The gap: the apt step carries NO step-level timeout and no retry. The pytest step has
both (timeout-minutes: 10 plus pytest's own --timeout, tests.yml:111); the two networked
installs that precede it have neither, so the only thing bounding them is the whole-job
cap they then consume.

Fix direction (bound the flaky operation, not the job):
  - give `Install system dependencies` its own timeout-minutes (~5) so a mirror stall
    fails in 5 minutes instead of eating 25;
  - retry apt-get update/install a couple of times with a short backoff — a stalled
    mirror is the textbook retryable failure;
  - same treatment for the npm ci step, which is the other networked install the
    line-45 comment names.
Do NOT "fix" this by raising the job cap; that makes every occurrence more expensive.
title: A stalled apt step burns the whole fast-tests budget and then reads as a TEST failure
